title: Create a hipped footprint roof over a footprint with a per-edge slope
task: Create a FootPrintRoof on a level from a rectangular footprint and make it a hip roof by giving every eave a slope. Uses Document.Create.NewFootPrintRoof(CurveArray, level, RoofType, out ModelCurveArray) and sets FootPrintRoof.DefinesSlope / SlopeAngle per model curve.

pitfalls.symptom: roof.SlopeAngle[mc] = 0.5 or treating SlopeAngle/DefinesSlope as a plain property will not compile, so it looks like there is no way to set a roof edge's slope.
pitfalls.cause: DefinesSlope and SlopeAngle are named INDEXED properties keyed by a ModelCurve; C# has no obj[key] syntax for a named indexed property, and describe_function prints them as the accessor pair 'bool get_DefinesSlope(ModelCurve); void set_DefinesSlope(ModelCurve, bool)' (and likewise for SlopeAngle).
pitfalls.fix: Call the accessors exactly as describe_function shows: roof.set_DefinesSlope(mc, true) and roof.set_SlopeAngle(mc, slope); read back with roof.get_DefinesSlope(mc) / roof.get_SlopeAngle(mc). SlopeAngle is rise-over-run (0.5 == 6:12), not an angle in radians.

pitfalls.symptom: NewFootPrintRoof throws or the profile is rejected when a CurveLoop (as used for Floor.Create) is passed.
pitfalls.cause: NewFootPrintRoof takes a CurveArray of the footprint curves, not a CurveLoop / IList<CurveLoop> like Floor.Create.
pitfalls.fix: Build the footprint as a CurveArray and Append each Line; keep all points at the level elevation Z.

pitfalls.symptom: Setting slope on the input Line objects, or on the footprint you passed in, has no effect on the roof.
pitfalls.cause: Slope is a property of the roof's own ModelCurves, returned via the out ModelCurveArray parameter, not of the Curve objects passed in.
pitfalls.fix: Capture the out ModelCurveArray from NewFootPrintRoof and iterate it to call set_DefinesSlope / set_SlopeAngle on each ModelCurve.

provenance.ref: submission staged in the connector outbox (VM), not filed as an issue; supersedes the submitter's first cut (id ...-per-edge-slope) whose only difference was a pre-#186 comment
